learningObjective: Enumerate the dependence conditions under which a loop can be parallelized across iterations.

canonicalClaims.claim: A loop is legally parallelizable across iterations when there are no cross-iteration output (WAW), true (RAW), or anti (WAR) dependences, or when such dependences are captured by an associative reduction clause with an appropriate combiner.
conditions: Statements are free of side effects outside of the reduction targets.
Reductions, if present, use an associative operator (or an explicit reduction clause).
nonImplications: Does not imply parallelization yields speedup; trip count, work per iteration, and hardware parallelism all matter.
Does not imply FP-associativity concerns can be ignored in numerically sensitive code.

misconceptions.claim: Any conditional inside the loop body makes parallelization illegal.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SIMT and multi-threaded parallelization handle conditionals via masking or thread-local branches; divergence is a performance issue, not a legality one.

misconceptions.claim: Parallelization requires a compile-time-known trip count.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Runtime trip counts are routinely parallelized (OpenMP `parallel for`, CUDA grid over `ceil(N/BLOCK)`).

misconceptions.claim: A reduction inside the loop always blocks parallelization because it creates a WAW dependence on the accumulator.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Reductions are parallelizable via associative combiners and per-thread partial accumulators.

misconceptions.claim: A cross-iteration write to distinct memory locations (`A[i]`) is a WAW dependence and blocks parallelization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Writing to `A[i]` (distinct per iteration) is not a WAW; WAW requires two iterations to write to the SAME location.

implementationFacts: OpenMP `#pragma omp parallel for reduction(+:s)` legalizes accumulator reductions.
CUDA blocks execute independently and rely on the compiler / programmer to enforce no cross-block dependences.
performanceScenarios: A histogram loop `h[a[i]] += 1` cannot be parallelized as-is (WAW on random locations); it requires atomics or per-thread private histograms.
